A crewed steel lander about 30 metres tall stands landed in the left third of the frame, turned three-quarters to the camera, not facing it head-on and not centred. The ground is bare grey regolith with small stones, the dust under the engine bells scoured out radially and slightly darker. One hard sun, low, about ten degrees above the ground, out of frame to the left. Every shadow runs the same way, long, sharp-edged and pure black, stretching to the right: the ship's shadow lies across the plain several times longer than the ship is tall, the legs, figures, tripod and stones each throw thin parallel shadows. The shadow side of the hull is very dark, lit only faintly from below by grey light thrown up from the ground. The sky is flat black with no stars, no Earth, no planet and no gradient, black all the way down to the horizon; the grey ground ends at a hard, sharp horizon line with no pale band, no glow and no haze. Camera held by a person standing about fifty metres away, at eye height, 35mm lens, verticals level and plumb, deep focus with the near tripod and the far horizon equally sharp. True colour, no added grain, no film border, no crosshair grid.
